description: Design a logger system that receives a stream of messages with timestamps. Each unique message should only be printed at most once every 10 seconds. Return true if the message should be printed, false otherwise.
intuition: Store the next allowed print time for each message in a hash map. When a message arrives, compare the timestamp against the stored value. If enough time has passed, allow it and update the next allowed time. Simple and O(1) per call.
approach: Use a hash map storing the next allowed timestamp for each message. If the current timestamp is >= the stored value, print the message and update the timestamp to current + 10.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: [[1,"foo"],[2,"bar"],[3,"foo"],[8,"bar"],[10,"foo"],[11,"foo"]]

t=1,  "foo": new → allow, nextAllowed["foo"]=11, return true
t=2,  "bar": new → allow, nextAllowed["bar"]=12, return true
t=3,  "foo": 3 < 11 → block, return false
t=8,  "bar": 8 < 12 → block, return false
t=10, "foo": 10 < 11 → block, return false
t=11, "foo": 11 >= 11 → allow, nextAllowed["foo"]=21, return true
explanation:
1. Maintain a dictionary mapping messages to their next allowed print time.
2. If the message is new or the current timestamp >= next allowed time, allow it.
3. Update the next allowed time to timestamp + 10.
4. Otherwise, reject the message.
hints: Use a hash map to store the last allowed print time for each message.
Compare the current timestamp against the stored time.
Update the stored time when the message is printed.
